name: uri-constraint-with-port-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees uniformResourceIdentifier is 'example.com:443' — the constraint carries a port number. RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10 specifies URI constraints as host-name forms ('any URI within the named host or its subdomains'); a port is not part of the host name space and embedding one in a constraint is undefined. The leaf's URI SAN 'foo://example.com:443/path' would match the host portion but the constraint itself is malformed. BoringSSL rejects this as UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRAINT_SYNTAX; lenient implementations that string-suffix-match might accept the leaf by accident, or might apply the port literally and reject the leaf if its port differs.
notes: Probes the constraint side specifically — most of the corpus's URI tests put exotic shapes on the SAN side and keep the constraint clean. Strict parsers should reject the CA's nameConstraints extension at parse time as soon as they see the colon-port in a URI constraint; lax parsers may attempt to match anyway.
